about: Divan's real routes: sea lanes (in the order ships travel them), pipelines (from source to terminal). Every feature says where it comes from and how exact it is. Positions are for a news map, never for navigation.

properties.en: Strait of Hormuz TSS, outbound (eastbound) lane
properties.source: IMO traffic separation scheme «In the Strait of Hormuz» (two 2-mile lanes with a 2-mile separation zone, north of the Musandam peninsula and the Quoin islands; right-hand traffic, so outbound is the southern lane). Digitised by hand from public chart depictions: the official coordinates are in IMO Ships' Routeing and Admiralty charts, not public. Accuracy about ±3 km.

properties.en: Strait of Hormuz TSS, inbound (westbound) lane
properties.source: IMO traffic separation scheme «In the Strait of Hormuz»: the northern lane, about 4 nautical miles (2 lane + 2 separation) north of the outbound lane. Digitised by hand from public chart depictions; accuracy about ±3 km.

properties.en: Red Sea main route (Suez to Bab el-Mandeb), southbound
properties.source: Divan's schematic lane on the main Red Sea route, mid-channel; not a charted scheme. Accuracy about ±20 km.

Route as published by NIOC and in news maps (Goreh near Genaveh, Bushehr province, to the Kuh-e Mobarak terminal west of Jask, about 1,000 km). Schematic along the published corridor; accuracy about ±15 km.

properties.fa: خط لولهٔ شرق به غرب عربستان
properties.source: Saudi Aramco's East–West crude pipeline from the Abqaiq area to Yanbu on the Red Sea, about 1,200 km. Schematic along the published corridor; accuracy about ±20 km.
ADNOC's Abu Dhabi Crude Oil Pipeline from Habshan to Fujairah on the Gulf of Oman, about 370 km. Schematic along the published corridor; accuracy about ±10 km.
